title: Design Stewardship Compass: Contribution Flow, Peer Review, and Retirement Policy
creator: Maya Chen
description: A single-source guide that defines how designers contribute to the Redwood design system, how proposals are reviewed, and how components or tokens are retired with minimal product disruption. This doc codifies a repeatable contribution flow, an actionable peer-review checklist tailored to tokens, interactive components (buttons, tables, charts), and an auditable retirement path (deprecation -> sunset -> migration). It is intended for designers, design engineers, and PMs collaborating on system changes.
acceptance_criteria: A clear step-by-step contribution flow is published and sharable in Confluence and the design system README
A peer-review checklist exists for tokens, layout components, interactive components, and charts and is used in at least 3 incoming PRs
An RFC template and living index are available and linked from the design system repo
A deprecation playbook with communication cadence and automated telemetry checks is approved
Owners for each component group (tokens, buttons, tables, charts) are assigned and listed in the team roster
contribution_flow: 1) Ideation: Designer drafts a compact proposal (1 page) describing problem, user impact, and trade-offs. Attach screenshots and minimal reproducible examples.
2) Triage: Submit ticket to the design triage board (label: ds-contrib). Triage coordinator assigns reviewers from component owners.

3) RFC (when scope > small tweak): If change affects API surface, variants, accessibility, or token schema, open an RFC using the design RFC template and post to #design-system for 7 business days of comment.
4) Prototype & Accessibility Review: Provide a Figma prototype and a11y notes (contrast ratios, keyboard nav). Run with assistive tech if interaction changes.
5) Implementation PR: Create PR in design-system repo with token changes separated from code where possible. Use feature flag for larger surface changes.

6) Design + Eng Review: At least one designer owner and one engineer reviewer sign off. Include perceptual diff screenshots for visual changes and benchmark notes for performance-sensitive components.
7) Merge, Canary, and Monitor: Merge behind a rollout flag. Observe metrics for 72 hours (error rate, rendering regressions, SLO signals) before enabling for all tenants.
8) Post-merge Documentation: Update component docs, migration notes, changelog entry, and link to the RFC and PRs. Add to release notes and console change log if applicable.
review_checklist: General: Is there an owner listed and a clear motivation for the change?
Design tokens: Are tokens named to reflect intent (semantic names preferred) and grouped by usage? Have aliases and fallback tokens been considered?
Accessibility: Contrast, focus order, ARIA roles, and keyboard support verified? Include screen-reader labels for non-text controls.
Responsiveness: Layout behavior documented for common breakpoints and density settings?
Backward compatibility: Will existing consumers be affected? Is migration path documented (codemod, token aliasing, compat layer)?
Performance: Any impact on render cost (tables/charts) or bundle size? Have lazy-loading or virtualization options been considered for tables/charts?
Testing: Are unit and snapshot tests included? Are visual regression tests added to the design-system test harness?
Docs: Examples for primary/secondary states, disabled, validation messages, and error states included? Is usage guidance present (do/don't, patterns)?
Internationalization: Do labels support i18n and layout for long strings or RTL?
Security & Privacy: Does the change introduce new telemetry or user data surfaces? If yes, coordinate with Security team.
rfc_process: When to file an RFC: Any change that (a) modifies public component API, (b) migrates or renames tokens, (c) affects accessibility or major UX patterns, or (d) has multi-team consequences.
Template: Use the design RFC template (Problem, Proposed Change, Alternatives, Backwards Compatibility, Rollout Plan, Test Plan, Owners). Keep RFC under 3 pages for review efficiency.
Review window: Post RFC to #design-system and the cross-functional RFC board for a 7-business-day comment period. Triage meeting will summarize unresolved objections.
Decision matrix: Approve (merge RFC), Request changes, Defer, or Reject. Approval requires at least two design owners and one engineering stakeholder from impacted teams.
Living index: RFCs numbered and indexed in Confluence. Link RFC number in PRs and changelogs. Maintain a change log of approved RFCs per release.
deprecation_policy: When to deprecate: Replace when a component or token is obsolete, harmful to accessibility, or creates maintenance burden.

Deprecation stages: Announcement (30 days), Soft-deprecation (announced but still available with warning), Sunset planning (document migration and codemod if applicable), Removal (minimum 90 days after announcement unless critical security/bug fix).
Communication: Email to internal stakeholders, console in-product banners for affected customers, changelog entry, and a migration guide in the design docs.
Compatibility flags: Provide alias tokens and a compat CSS layer for at least one release cycle where feasible. Track usage across repos to prioritize migration assistance.

Telemetry and rollback: Before removal, validate no active customers depend on the API using telemetry. If significant usage exists, extend deprecation timeline and offer engineering support. Always provide a rollback plan for critical regressions.
rollout_and_communication: Internal: Add to the weekly design sync agenda and the DS triage board. Notify support and solutions teams four business days before broad rollout.
External: For public/enterprise customers, include deprecation notices in the console and send targeted migration playbooks where usage is detected.
Training: Host a 30-minute walkthrough for engineers and PMs on substantive surface changes and list office hours for migration help.
audit_and_metrics: Ownership: Maintain a roster mapping component groups to owners in Confluence and the design system README.
Metrics: Track PR lead time, time to merge, number of backcompat incidents, and visual regression failures per release.
Postmortems: Any deprecation that caused user impact requires a brief postmortem linked from the original ticket.
notes: This doc purposely separates token changes from component implementation to reduce churn across repos.
Consider a monthly 'maintenance window' sprint for low-risk token consolidations to keep tech debt bounded.
Follow-up work: create a lightweight codemod playbook for token renames (ENG-2941).
Open question: Should we add a 'signature' badge on approved RFCs to indicate cross-functional sign-off? Tentatively yes; discuss in design sync.
